newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan May index of leading indicators rises.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan May index of leading indicators rises.

text.p: Taiwan's index of leading business indicators, which forecasts peaks and troughs in the business cycle, rose in May, showing gradual economic recovery, Taiwan's top economic planning agency said on Friday.
The index, fueled by export and industrial output growth, increased 0.4 percent to 103.5 in May from April, the Cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development said in a statement.
The index of coincident indicators, however, dropped one percent to 101.1 from April on reduction of domestic cargo and bills exchange volume, the agency said.
The council said the economy in May remained in a "green light" condition for the seventh straight month, indicating a gradual recovery.
"The seventh consecutive green light shows (the) domestic economy maintains a steady growth," the statement said.

Sixteen percent of a sample poll of manufacturing executives said the economy would turn worse in the next three months, down from 15 percent in April, while 19 percent said the economy would improve, up from 18 percent a month earlier.
The rest said the economy would remain unchanged.
Analysts generally concur that Taiwan's economy is enjoying a modest recovery, spurred by improving export orders and healthy domestic consumption.
